passage:
Text 1
Many researchers attribute the decline of honeybee colonies chiefly to neonicotinoid pesticides, which can impair bees' navigation. Some field studies have found that colonies near treated crops produce fewer new queens.

Text 2
Entomologist Dana Whitfield argues that focusing on any single cause is misleading. In her surveys, colonies exposed to pesticides suffered most when they were also infested with parasitic mites and short of diverse food sources. Remove the mites and add varied flowers, she found, and the same pesticide exposure did far less harm.
stem: Based on the texts, how would Whitfield (Text 2) most likely respond to the researchers in Text 1?
choices: By arguing that pesticides matter mainly in combination with other stresses on colonies
By claiming that neonicotinoid pesticides cause no harm to honeybee colonies at all
By agreeing that pesticides are the chief cause of colony decline in most regions
By suggesting that colonies near treated crops should produce more new queens
steps: Text 1: pesticides are the chief cause.
Text 2: harm is worst when pesticides combine with mites and poor food; without those, the same exposure did less harm.
So Whitfield would say pesticides matter mainly together with other stresses.
She doesn't say they cause no harm, doesn't agree they're the chief cause, and says nothing about queen numbers.
key: Describe Text 2's view precisely; it often qualifies Text 1 rather than flatly rejecting it.
